newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay index rebounds as political hopes brighten.
newsitem.headline: Bombay index rebounds as political hopes brighten.

text.p: Share prices rebounded in Friday afternoon trade on news the United Front coalition, which faced certain defeat in parliament, and its former ally the Congress party began talks to break the political stalemate and avert snap polls, brokers said.
The Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) top-30 share index jumped 45.87 points, or 1.27 percent, to 3,644.24 after sliding to 3,512.05 in early trade.
Coalition and Congress leaders told Reuters a consensus candidate for prime minister's job could be named by the United Front before a parliamentary trust vote later on Friday.
"We are expecting a change in leadership," Hannan Mollah, a deputy of the Communist Party of India-Marxist said.
Congress deputies said a deal was being worked out to avoid elections, which politicians said could be held by June if the impasse continues.
"Either before the vote or after, a new leader will be chosen, said Jayanthi Natarajan, a Congress deputy. "We believe the United front has already named its candidate," she said without elaborating.
The widely acclaimed business-friendly budget for 1997/98 (April-March) may survive the political crisis, Finance Minister P. Chidambaram said.
"As parliamentarians, it is possible to get together to pass the Finance Bill irrespective of the difficulties which the executive faces," he told reporters.
